historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is undefined: shareholders' equity has been negative every year since 2011 (securitisation-funded buybacks), so the house default anchor cannot be used. EPS CAGR (7-12%) runs well above revenue (3-4%) because of the shrinking share count (39.6M diluted FY2020 -> 33.3M) and margin gains; it overstates the growth of the business. Revenue 5-yr CAGR selected.
historical_growth.notes: Bases (SEC XBRL, correct fiscal years): revenue FY2020 4,117.4 / FY2022 4,537.2 / FY2025 4,940.0; diluted EPS 12.39 / 12.53 / 17.57; owner FCF (OCF - capex - SBC - equity-award taxes) FY2020 473.0 / FY2022 ~352.4 (equity-award taxes ~7 estimated) / FY2025 615.5. The 3-yr FCF CAGR (~20%) starts from a FY2022 working-capital/inflation trough and ends at a FY2025 peak (OCF +27% on +5% revenue), so it is not a growth rate to extrapolate; the 5-yr 5.4% is the cleaner read. Owner FCF CAGR is ~0.5pp below reported on the 5-yr, i.e. SBC + withholding (24.2+6.8 -> 44.6+11.4) has grown faster than cash flow. All FCF figures are levered (post ~$185M cash interest).

scenario_narratives.base: US comps recover from the H1 FY2026 0.1-0.9% trough to low single digits as the loyalty programme (37M active members), the new e-commerce platform and the DoorDash marketplace channel offset a soft consumer, while weaker rivals (Pizza Hut's ~250 US closures, Papa John's) cede share. International adds ~800 net stores a year but DPE's Japan/Europe closures keep international comps near flat for another year or two. Revenue compounds ~3.8% (the 5-yr history), adj. EBITDA margin edges from 22.0% to 22.8% on supply-chain volume leverage, capex stays ~2.4% of revenue. The Joe Jordan CEO transition is continuity, not a pivot.
scenario_narratives.bull: Share gains accelerate: the pizza category consolidates toward Domino's as competitors shrink, delivery order frequency recovers with consumer sentiment, and loyalty/app economics lift US comps to 3-4%. DPE completes its restructuring and international royalty growth returns to mid-single digits on ~4% unit growth. Supply-chain centres run at higher utilisation, pushing adj. EBITDA margin to 24% by FY2031, and a durable franchisor with 5%+ growth earns a 20x terminal multiple at 3% perpetual growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: The value war persists: US comps stay near zero, delivery keeps declining, franchisee four-wall margins are squeezed by labour and food inflation, and Domino's has to concede supply-chain margin and fund promotions to protect franchisee economics, taking adj. EBITDA margin down to 21%. DPE's distress spreads to further closures and slower international development; unit growth halves to ~2%. Capex rises to 2.6% as supply-chain and technology investment continues regardless. Refinancing of securitised tranches at higher coupons does not change unlevered value but caps capital returns. A 2%-growth franchisor gets 14x at exit.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Domino's is valued as an unlevered, asset-light franchisor/distributor: component-built owner FCF (SBC and equity-award withholding fully expensed, share count flat) discounted at a 7.5% USD WACC, with the full $4.9B securitised debt deducted once in the equity bridge. Negative book equity is a financing choice, so book-value anchors are ignored and revenue CAGR is the growth anchor. The price sits after a ~30% 2026 de-rating on weak US comps; the question the model answers is whether a ~4% grower with 14-15% owner-FCF margins is worth more than ~17x forward unlevered FCF.
key_risks_to_valuation: US same-store sales stay near zero (H1 FY2026 0.1-0.9%): the bear path (2% growth, 21% margin, 14x exit) is worth $170/share, 42% below the price
Domino's Pizza Enterprises distress drags international royalties and unit growth
Leverage: $4.9B securitised debt against ~$9.7B market cap makes equity value ~1.5x as sensitive to EV as an unlevered peer

Discount rate: the 18x terminal cap binds at WACC <= 7.5%, so terminal growth barely moves the base value, but each 1pp of WACC moves it ~$45-65/share (8.5% -> $260, 6.5% -> $340); terminal value is ~60% of base EV
Excluded restricted/ad-fund cash (~$4-6/share) and the FY2026 53rd week are both small but move FY2026-27 optics
Metrics.csv FY2021/FY2022 rows are mislabelled by one fiscal year and FY2022 is missing - dashboard history charts will show a shifted series until the parser fixes it

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 282.00-442.35
data_sources.financials: DPZ_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL) for FY2023-Q2 FY2026; SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 1286681) for FY2020-FY2022 revenue/EPS/OCF/capex (CSV rows mislabelled), income taxes paid, interest paid, finance-lease and operating-lease liabilities, restricted cash, diluted weighted shares Q2 FY2026
data_sources.qualitative: DPZ_Analysis.json (2026-09), FY2026 guidance as reaffirmed with Q2 FY2026 results (July 2026)

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 FY2026 10-Q (12 weeks to 2026-06-14), 33,318,244; held FLAT because SBC (plus equity-award withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows. DPZ is a heavy repurchaser (FY2025 $357.7M, H1 FY2026 $234.6M, ~8-10x SBC), so the flat count is funded many times over; the excess buyback is a use of the owner FCF already inside the valuation, not extra value.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement: stock-based compensation 44.64 + taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards 11.36 (financing) = 56.0. DPZ publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line, so the two lines are summed. H1 FY2026 runs hotter (SBC 21.1 + withholding 12.9 = 1.45% of revenue), hence the FY2026 path starts at 1.3%.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Sunday closest to 31 December (52/53-week); FY2025 ended 2025-12-28, FY2026 ends 2027-01-03 and is a 53-week year
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build. Cost of equity: 10-yr UST ~4.2% + levered beta 1.0 x 5.0% ERP = 9.2%. Cost of debt: securitised whole-business notes carry 2.7-7.6% coupons (blended ~4%), but tranches refinance at today's ~5.5%, after tax (22.5%) ~4.3%. Market weights E ~9.7B (66%) / D ~4.9B (34%) -> 7.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is carried in the driver paths and the 25% bear weight, not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating-lease cost (~$232M operating lease liabilities) sits inside EBITDA as rent, so operating leases are NOT in net debt. Finance-lease obligations ($125.9M at 2026-06-14, up from $62.0M at FY2025 year-end on new supply-chain facilities) are inside total_debt 4,883.6 and deducted there once; lease_cost_pct_path is therefore 0.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing row: operating company - asset-light franchisor plus US/Canada supply-chain distributor). Negative shareholders' equity (-3.98B at 2026-06-14) is an artefact of recapitalisations via whole-business securitisation that funded buybacks; it is not distress and makes book-value methods meaningless, so the unlevered EV route with the full securitised debt deducted is the right frame. Flows are UNLEVERED (EBIT-based cash tax, no interest), so the ~$185M/yr of cash interest inside reported FCF is NOT deducted again - the debt is charged once, in net_debt. last_fcf (615.5 = 671.5 reported - 56.0 SBC incl. withholding) is a LEVERED reference figure; the unlevered FY2025 owner FCF on the component build is ~ $700M. interest_income set 0 because the company is heavily net-indebted (interest income 14.9 in FY2025 is on restricted/ad-fund cash). CASH: only unrestricted cash (164.8) counted; restricted cash (securitisation interest reserves ~$146-216M) and advertising-fund cash (belongs to the franchisee ad fund) are excluded - conservative by ~$4-6/share. 53-WEEK YEAR: FY2026 includes a 53rd week (~1.5-2pp of revenue), reversed in FY2027 growth. DATA WARNING for the financial-parser: Metrics.csv rows FY2021 and FY2022 are one fiscal year shifted (the 'FY2021' row is FY2020, 53 weeks to 2021-01-03; 'FY2022' is FY2021 to 2022-01-02) and the true FY2022 (to 2023-01-01: revenue 4,537.2, NI 452.3, OCF 475.3, capex 87.2) is missing. Historical CAGRs below are computed from SEC XBRL companyfacts on correct fiscal years, not from the mislabelled rows.

base.growth_note: FY2026 5.0% = H1 +3.9% plus the 53rd week (~1.7pp) in Q4; FY2027 2.5% laps it. Then ~3.8% (global unit growth ~3.5% + low-single US comps, supply-chain pass-through pricing), fading to 3.0%. Matches the 3.7% 5-yr revenue CAGR.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Adj. EBITDA before SBC: FY2025 (1,042.8 + 44.6)/4,940 = 22.0%; H1 FY2026 22.4%. Guidance of mid-to-high single-digit operating-income growth on ~4-5% revenue implies modest leverage; +0.1pp/yr to 22.8%.
base.wc_note: Supply-chain receivables and inventory from franchisees exceed payables modestly; growth consumes a little cash.
base.tax_note: FY2025 GAAP ETR 21.9%, cash taxes paid 161.9 on ~770 pretax (21%); 22.5% on unlevered EBIT (federal + state, less FDII/excess-benefit variability).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: US comps have missed for two consecutive quarters against a reaffirmed low-single-digit target, the largest master franchisee (DPE) is in distress, and a CEO transition lands on 1 Oct 2026 - the downside axis is live, not hypothetical (the securitised fixed-rate debt means it is an earnings risk, not a solvency one). Base 50% as the reaffirmed guidance path. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things - US comp recovery, DPE stabilisation and sustained margin expansion - to go right together.
